sections.label: Inspector qualifications and director declaration
sections.summary: The speaker declares being a director of three SkillsFuture-funded course providers and asks the Minister about qualifications to be an appointed inspector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the outset, I would like to declare that I am a director of three institutions that provide SkillsFuture-funded courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, regarding the appointment of inspectors, I would like to ask the Minister what the qualifications are to be an appointed inspector?

sections.label: Advertisement definition and marketing forms
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Bill captures other marketing forms like roadshows or in-person hard selling, given the narrow advertisement definition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, the definition of "advertisement" in article 57(E) seems relatively narrow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I should be grateful if the Minister could address how the Bill captures other forms of marketing, such as roadshows or in-person hard selling.

sections.label: Commission-based recruitment agents for training
sections.summary: The speaker says training providers should not be allowed to engage commission-based recruitment agents for any SkillsFuture-funded courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There should be no room for unscrupulous agents to profit from Government-funded training programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And in my humble opinion, Mr Speaker, training providers should not be allowed to engage commission-based recruitment agents for any SkillsFuture-funded courses.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit usage by Singaporeans
sections.summary: Minister Chan said 840,000 Singapore citizens have used SkillsFuture Credit since its introduction, which is only 30% of eligible Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This is only possible through collaboration with education and training partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, I am glad to hear from Minister Chan in the November Parliamentary Sitting that since the introduction of SkillsFuture, 840,000 Singapore citizens have utilised their SkillsFuture Credit (SFC).

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, that is only 30% of eligible Singaporeans.

sections.label: SkillsFuture scam and Bill support
sections.summary: The speaker cites the $40 million SkillsFuture scam by Ng Cheng Hwee and Lee Lai Leng and supports the Bill to strengthen regulatory powers against fraud.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, some have taken the opportunity to abuse the funding arrangements such as the case of the husband and wife masterminds, Ng Cheng Hwee and Lee Lai Leng, who were behind the $40 million SkillsFuture scam by submitting and forging falsified documents between May and August 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, I stand in support of this Bill to strengthen the regulatory powers of SkillsFuture against fraud and abuse of its incentives and grants.

sections.label: SkillsFuture credit usage and age gap
sections.summary: More than 840,000 Singaporeans used SkillsFuture credits since 2015, only 30% of eligible, with highest utilisation among younger ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Since its launch in 2015, more than 840,000 Singaporeans have used their SkillsFuture credits to take up skills upgrading courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, this figure represents only 30% of those eligible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This means that 70% of eligible Singaporeans have yet to use their SkillsFuture credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: What is more worrisome, its utilisation is highest among the younger ones, compared to those who are 40 years and above.

sections.label: False government recognition claims
sections.summary: The member seeks clarifications on circumstances where training providers falsely indicate their courses are recognised by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: (In English): Hence, I would like to seek clarifications regarding circumstances in which training providers falsely indicate that their courses are recognised by the Government.

sections.label: IT gadgets baiting elderly
sections.summary: The member asks whether the Government received complaints about training providers using IT gadgets to bait elderly Singaporeans into signing up for IT courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Has the Government received complaints about training providers using IT gadgets to bait elderly Singaporeans to sign up for IT courses?

sections.label: Suspension notices against training operators
sections.summary: The member asks whether the Ministry will share how many suspension notices have been issued against errant training operators since 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry share how many suspension notices have been issued against errant training operators since 2016?

sections.label: Adult Educators Qualifications Requirements
sections.summary: SkillsFuture Singapore sets out Adult Educators Qualifications Requirements for training providers offering SSG-funded certifiable courses to raise adult training quality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To raise the quality of adult training and education in Singapore, SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) sets out Adult Educators (AE) Qualifications Requirements that apply to training providers providing SSG-funded certifiable courses.

sections.label: Offence of false advertising
sections.summary: The new section 57E amended by the SSG Bill makes it an offence to publish false or misleading advertising.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 57E amended by the SSG Bill will make it an offence to publish false or misleading advertising.

sections.label: Fraud detection after 2017 case
sections.summary: In Public Prosecutor vs Ng Cheng Kwee, the Prosecution described most fraudulent claims as automatically approved by SSG, and after the 2017 fraud SSG announced in 2018 it strengthened fraud detection using data analytics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the case of Public Prosecutor vs Ng Cheng Kwee, the Prosecution described most of the fraudulent claims as having been "automatically approved by SSG" and that only "a small proportion of the claims were flagged for a manual check".

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Following this incident of fraud which occurred in 2017, the SSG announced in 2018 that it has strengthened its fraud detection systems using data analytics.

sections.label: Deferred payment for SkillsFuture courses
sections.summary: The Minister is asked whether the Ministry has looked into a deferred payment model for certain SkillsFuture courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can Minister share if the Ministry has looked into such a deferred payment model for certain SkillsFuture courses?

sections.label: New offences and SSG powers
sections.summary: The Bills prescribe new offences for abusive funding arrangements and let SSG recover funds, act on false advertisements, and appoint authorised persons and inspectors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: One of the key amendments in these Bills is the prescription of new offences related to "abusive funding arrangements" and the power for SSG to recover its funds or take action against false advertisements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In addition, the amendment will allow SSG to appoint authorised persons and inspectors who would have greater investigative power and conduct enforcement actions.

sections.label: Concern for small businesses
sections.summary: One concern is that the amendments may disproportionately affect small businesses and organisations lacking resources to defend against enforcement actions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: One concern is that the amendments may disproportionately affect small businesses and organisations, as they may not have the resources to defend themselves against enforcement actions.

sections.label: Clarity in enforcement process
sections.summary: Another concern is the need for clarity, transparency and accountability in the enforcement process.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Another concern is the need for clarity, transparency and accountability in the enforcement process.

sections.label: Support with question on SSG officers
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bills but asks whether the proposed new powers are to be given to all SSG officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I therefore support the proposals in the Bills to strengthen SSG's funding and schemes which will serve to enhance the credibility of adult learning programmes as a whole.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: However, given the enhanced powers of SSG officers to enter premises, search for and seize documents, and to conduct interviews, I would like to ask if the proposed new powers are to be given to all SSG officers.

sections.label: Courses losing funding status
sections.summary: The question asks the average number of courses that had their funding status removed due to poor sign-ups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: What is the average number of courses that had their funding status removed due to poor sign-ups?

sections.label: Abuse of SSG funding
sections.summary: Examples of abuse include false claims of government recognition, bogus course claims, and companies submitting claims for employees who only attended courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: We have heard about examples of such abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: We have training providers falsely indicating that the Government recognises their courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: We have bogus claims being submitted for courses that were not conducted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: We have multiple companies where claims were submitted to SSG for employees whose only role and job was to attend SSG-funded courses.

sections.label: SSG participation and training providers
sections.summary: In 2021 about 660,000 individuals and 24,000 enterprises benefited from SSG programmes, with 25 Queen Bee companies and close to 1,000 training providers offering about 25,000 courses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In 2021, about 660,000 individuals and 24,000 enterprises participated in and benefited from SSG-supported programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Companies have also leaned forward to drive skills development, with 25 SkillsFuture Queen Bee companies partnering SSG to uplift skills in their respective sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: There are now close to 1,000 training providers, providing about 25,000 courses supported by SSG.

sections.label: Recovering SDL underpayments
sections.summary: SSG has contacted all affected employers to reconcile variances and is recovering underpayments of the SDL.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: As for recovering underpayment of the SDL which I had previously touched on in Parliament, SSG has contacted all affected employers to reconcile the variances and is in the process of recovering the underpayments.

sections.label: Training provider liability for false ads
sections.summary: A training provider may be liable if the Court finds it knew, ought to have known, or was reckless as to whether an advertisement was false or misleading.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The training provider may be held liable if the Court ascertains that the training provider had known or ought to reasonably have known that the advertisement is false or misleading or has been reckless as to whether the advertisement is false or misleading.

sections.label: Statutory presumption for abusive arrangements
sections.summary: The statutory presumption applies when the first two elements are present and steps were taken to obtain SSG funding, putting the onus on the accused to show no dishonest intent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: And third, they must have entered into or facilitated the abusive funding arrangement with the intention to dishonestly or fraudulently induce SSG to provide funding to them, or to someone else.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: It is only when the first two elements are present and when it is proven that the person has taken steps to help the person or someone else obtain funding from SSG, that the statutory presumption comes into effect to put the onus on the person charged with the offence to demonstrate that he did not have dishonest or fraudulent intentions.

sections.label: Recovered funds returned to source
sections.summary: Recovered funds would be paid back to the funds they were drawn from to support upskilling efforts, responding to Assoc Prof Jamus Lim's concern about perverse incentives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim said that the amendments seem to allow for the wrongly obtained funds recovered by SSG to be channelled towards funding is operational costs and that this could create potentially perverse incentives for over-zealous regulation and possible abuse.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: They would be paid back to the funds they were drawn from so that they can be used for the intended purpose, which is to support upskilling efforts.

sections.label: Survey not aiding investigations
sections.summary: The survey is not done with investigations and its questions are not designed to aid investigations into abuse of SSG's funding.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The survey is not done in conjunction with investigations and questions are not designed with the intent of aiding investigations into abuse of SSG's funding.

sections.label: Investigative powers match offences
sections.summary: The principle is that investigative powers should be commensurate with the nature of the offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Broadly, the principle is that investigative powers should be commensurate with the nature of the offences.

sections.label: Inspector must show SSG card
sections.summary: An inspector must produce the identification card issued by SSG before exercising powers under the Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: For instance, an inspector must produce the identification card issued by SSG before they can exercise powers under the Act.

sections.label: Court decides penalties within limits
sections.summary: The penalties will be decided by the Court, within the limits stipulated in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The penalties will be decided by the Court, within the limits stipulated in the Bill.

sections.label: Strengthening SSG's legislative levers
sections.summary: Strengthening SSG's legislative levers is important to deter errant behaviour and preserve public confidence and trust in the training system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: As the Government continues to ramp up our investments in SkillsFuture and prepare for the future economy, it is important for us to strengthen SSG's legislative levers so as to deter errant behaviour as well as to preserve public confidence and trust in the training system.

sections.label: Sitting suspended for Second Reading
sections.summary: Sitting was suspended at 4.02 pm until 4.25 pm, with the formal Second Reading of the SDL (Amendment) Bill still to come.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.02 pm until 4.25 pm.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: We will still have the formal Second Reading of the SDL (Amendment) Bill to ensure that the procedural requirements are dealt with.

sections.label: SSG funding abuse offences
sections.summary: The SSG (Amendment) Bill creates offences against abuse of SSG funding and misrepresentation of SSG funding schemes, courses and providers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: To address these issues, the SSG (Amendment) Bill creates specific offences against the abuse of SSG funding, as well as misrepresentation of SSG's funding schemes, SSG-funded courses and SSG-funded providers.

sections.label: Abusive funding arrangement offence
sections.summary: Clause 12 inserts section 57B defining an abusive funding arrangement and setting out the offence's elements and penalties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: First, clause 12 inserts section 57B to define "abusive funding arrangement" as one where a person obtains funding that they would not have gotten or higher than what they would have otherwise gotten from SSG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The key elements of the new offence are as follows: (a) the offenders must have entered into or facilitated an abusive funding arrangement which I have just described; (b) they must have known or have had reason to believe that the funding arrangement is abusive in nature; and (c) they must have entered into or facilitated the abusive funding arrangement, with the intention to dishonestly or fraudulently induce SSG to provide funding to them or to someone else.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Those convicted of this offence will be liable for a penalty equal to the amount that they wrongly obtained, or would have wrongly obtained and a fine and/or imprisonment.

sections.label: False or misleading advertisements offence
sections.summary: Clause 12 inserts section 57E creating an offence for false or misleading advertisements, including false claims of SSG funding, approval or endorsement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Second, clause 12 inserts the new section 57E to set out a specific offence for publication or distribution of an advertisement that is false or misleading in a material way.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Subsection 4 under the new section 57E defines a "false or misleading advertisement" as an advertisement that falsely represents that SSG has provided funding, approval or endorsement for a course or its provider when this is not the case.

sections.label: Deterring false advertisements
sections.summary: The new false or misleading advertisements offence will allow SSG to take actions to deter such activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The new offence of "false or misleading advertisements" will allow the SSG to take actions to deter such activities.

sections.label: SSG refund directions
sections.summary: Clause 12 inserts section 57G empowering SSG to direct training providers and funding recipients to refund monies if a course does not start or is not completed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: In addition, to better safeguard public interests, clause 12 inserts the new section 57G to empower SSG to direct training providers and other recipients of SSG funding to refund monies paid by trainees and/or funding provided by SSG if the course did not start on the scheduled start date or ceases to be provided before it is completed.

sections.label: Court repayment orders
sections.summary: Clause 13 inserts subsection 4 under section 58 empowering the Court to order convicted persons to repay wrongly obtained funds to SSG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Clause 13 will insert subsection 4 under section 58 to empower the Court to order those convicted of the offence to repay the wrongly obtained funds to SSG.

sections.label: Consolidating SSG funding offences
sections.summary: Offences and enforcement powers for SSG funding will be consolidated in the SSG Act for consistent application across funding sources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: First, because SSG currently taps on various funding sources, including SDF and other sources, we intend to consolidate offences and enforcement powers relating to the funding provided by SSG within the SSG Act, so that the offences and enforcement powers can be applied consistently, regardless of the funding source.

sections.label: Porting SDF offences to SSG Act
sections.summary: Offences for SSG funding paid wholly or partly from SDF monies will move from the SDL Act to the SSG Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Offences relating to SSG funding, paid wholly or partly out of SDF monies, will be ported over to the SSG Act from the SDL Act, and will be enforced using enforcement powers under the SSG Act.

sections.label: Redefining remuneration as wages
sections.summary: Clause 2 replaces the SDL Act definition of remuneration with the CPF Act definition of wages, leaving SDL computation and employee scope unchanged.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Clause 2 of the SDL (Amendment) Bill will replace the definition of "remuneration" in the SDL Act with a definition of "wages" as in the CPF Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The computation formula for SDL and the scope of employees for whom SDL is payable, remain unchanged.

sections.label: Elaborate funding abuse cases observed
sections.summary: Increased CET expenditure and landscape expansion have revealed funding abuse cases beyond current SSG and SDL acts, such as false Government recognition claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: With increased CET expenditure and expansion of the CET landscape, we have observed increasingly elaborate funding abuse cases that extend beyond the current purview of the existing SSG and SDL acts such as: One, training providers falsely indicating that its courses are recognised by the Government, or that they are free when, in fact, individuals need to use their SkillsFuture Credit to pay for out-of-pocket fees.

sections.label: Three fraudulent claims since 2016
sections.summary: Since its inception in 2016, SSG has encountered three unrelated cases of fraudulent claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Since its inception in 2016, SSG has encountered three unrelated cases of fraudulent claims.

sections.label: Penalties and SSG Act amendments
sections.summary: False or misleading information carries up to 12 months' imprisonment, a $10,000 fine, or both, under amendments targeting funding abuse and misleading advertisements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Persons who provide false or misleading information will be guilty of an offence, punishable at up to 12 months' imprisonment, or a fine up to $10,000 or both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to the SSG Act aim to target these shortfalls and shortcomings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: It aims to do this by designating abusive funding arrangements and misleading advertisements as an offence, allowing SSG to direct errant persons to make refunds and to expand SSG's scope of investigative powers.

sections.label: SSG inspector investigative powers conditions
sections.summary: The passage calls for clarification on the conditions for exercising investigative powers vested in SSG inspectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Additionally, there should be clarification on the conditions for exercising the investigative powers that are vested in SSG inspectors.

sections.label: SSG investigation time and punishment review
sections.summary: The passage asks how long SSG investigations take on average and whether punishments will be reviewed regularly, and supports the amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: With these enhanced powers, how long will SSG take before they complete an investigation, on average, for any offence or possible offence?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In a similar vein, will the punishments now set out in this Bill, be reviewed regularly and if so, how regularly to ensure it provides a deterring effect on would-be perpetrators, especially if scams and fraudulent schemes become more complex and egregious?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: To conclude, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, I rise in support of these amendments to strengthen SSG's regulatory powers to ensure that it remains fit for purpose and to achieve greater deterrence in preventing and remedying funding abuse, and inhibiting false or misleading advertising, which could damage public perception of SSG and the entire SkillsFuture initiative.

sections.label: AGO overpayments versus attempted fraud
sections.summary: The passage states the AGO report estimated overpayments of about $4.2 million over three years, against one attempted fraud case of $40 million over 14 years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To provide yet more context, the AGO report itself had estimated overpayments of around $4.2 million, over the course of three years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is a comparatively small fraction of the between $670 and $870 million provided for the agency in its budget.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This, of course, should be contrasted against reported cases of attempted fraud, which in one instance, amounted to $40 million over 14 years.

sections.label: SDL Act remuneration definition alignment
sections.summary: Clause 2 aligns the definition of "remuneration" in section 2 of the SDL Act with "wages" in section 2(1) of the CPF Act.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 2 of the proposed amendments to the SDL Act will align the definition of "remuneration" in section 2 of the Act with that of "wages" defined in section 2(1) of the CPF Act.

sections.label: Funding cut for non-certifiable courses
sections.summary: The Ministry will eliminate funding for non-certifiable courses less relevant to industry beginning in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To best calibrate courses with the demand side and hence, mitigate the risk I mentioned earlier, that courses become more a form of consumption rather than investment, the Ministry has stated that it will eliminate funding for non-certifiable courses that are less relevant to industry, beginning in 2025.

sections.label: ACLP hours, fee and subsidies
sections.summary: The original ACLP required almost 130 hours and the 2.0 version about 89 hours, with a $5,940 fee and subsidies including 90% for mid-career Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The original ACLP programme required almost 130 hours, while the 2.0 version still requires about 89 hours.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The fee is a non-trivial $5,940, although I would happily note that SSG is fully internally consistent and provides Singaporeans and PR with generous subsidies, including 90% funding for mid-career Singaporeans.

sections.label: In-house training scheme wound down
sections.summary: The in-house training providers scheme was wound down in October 2022 and in-house training ends from 2025.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The scheme that allows for in-house training providers was wound down in October 2022 and in-house training will no longer be available from 2025 onwards.

sections.label: Skilled practitioners and national apprenticeship
sections.summary: The question asks how many skilled practitioners qualified under this pathway and whether the AOP is envisioned as a national apprenticeship programme.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Would the Minister be willing to share with the House how many skilled practitioners have already qualified under this pathway and if the AOP is being envisioned as the basis of a more fully-fledged national apprenticeship programme?

sections.label: Incentives for existing employers
sections.summary: The passage asks about the agency's plans to strengthen incentives for existing employers to encourage SkillsFuture credit use, and supports the Bills.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is, of course, the topic of another speech.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But one common feedback we often hear is – how we can reduce the opportunity costs of individuals who are concurrently working, rather than those who have already separated from a job, so that they also receive incentives to pursue such upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What are the agency's plans to strengthen incentives for existing employers to encourage SkillsFuture credit use, if it is revealed to them that their employees are indeed under-utilising them?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These Bills before the House today are important common sense steps to improve the functioning of the system, and for that reason, they have my support.

sections.label: Criminal syndicate cheated SSG
sections.summary: A criminal syndicate in 2017 cheated SSG of $40 million in training grants through financial arrangements and forged documents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The most infamous abuse is that of a criminal syndicate in 2017, who cheated SSG of $40 million in training grants, through a series of complicated financial arrangements and forged documents.

sections.label: Penalties for wrongly obtained funding
sections.summary: An errant party may pay a penalty equal to the wrongly obtained funding, be fined up to $10,000, imprisoned up to three years, and/or ordered to repay.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: An errant party guilty of the offence would be punished in three ways – pay a penalty equal to the amount of the wrongly obtained funding; or fined not exceeding $10,000; and/or imprisonment for not exceeding three years; and/or ordered to repay the wrongly obtained funding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For instance, is a fine of $10,000, plus imprisonment, sufficient to deter a potential gain of $10 million?

sections.label: Inspectors insufficient for governance
sections.summary: With over 1,000 training providers and 25,000 SSG-supported courses, no number of SSG-appointed inspectors will ensure better governance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: With more than 1,000 training providers and 25,000 SSG-supported courses, no number of SSG-appointed inspectors will be enough to ensure better governance.

sections.label: Future of work and education
sections.summary: The future of work and education will feature mass customisation, tighter industry-academia tie-ups and lifelong education resources, and the adult training market needs further study and streamlining.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The future of work and education will be a landscape characterised by mass customisation, by tighter industry academia tie-ups and by spreading education resources throughout one's lifespan, and not only front-loaded in the first 15 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Its initial open and flexible strategy, for example, to encourage as many training and training providers as possible – and that is what Assoc Prof Jamus Lim is trying to encourage – this may be necessary in the first instance, but it has also led to SSG's support of a number of less than competent, and worse, dishonest training providers, due to the sheer size of the market that was created.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: More importantly, the current strategies may not sufficiently address critical motivation and training gaps of Singaporeans, such as the middle-aged workforce, such as the disabled, such as those who should, and can, take up better jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The adult education and training market needs to be further studied and further streamlined.

sections.label: SSG grant overpayment
sections.summary: Last year SSG overpaid approximately $4.2 million of grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)

sections.label: Recovery of owed SDL funds
sections.summary: The passage asks whether recovery provisions in proposed section 57D(2)(b) are adequate, noting an estimated $43 million of SDL still owed to SSG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With regard to repayment of owed funds, are the provisions for recovery set out in proposed section 57D(2)(b) of the proposed Bill adequate?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I note that an estimated $43 million of the SDL is still being owed to SSG.

sections.label: Priority for SSG debts
sections.summary: The passage raises how recovered funds should be divided among creditors and says debts owed to SSG should be given priority over other creditors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For instance, these include the issue of how recovered funds should be divided amongst various creditors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: These funds are important for the foremost reason that the funds belong to Singaporeans and are necessary in supporting workforce upgrading, as we increase our focus on CET.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I believe the recovery of such wrongly disbursed funding should be made as seamless as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Such debts owed to SSG should also be given priority over other creditors.

sections.label: SkillsFuture amendments adult learning providers
sections.summary: Proposed SkillsFuture amendments increase regulatory power over adult learning providers, supporting lifelong learning and public confidence in education quality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to SkillsFuture will certainly support citizens in their lifelong learning journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: By increasing the regulatory power over adult learning providers, it gives more certitude to the public on the quality and integrity of Singapore as an education hub.
